## `open_file_range` [#open_file_range]

Opens the pack stored whole in `length` bytes at `offset` of the file at `path` (memory-mapped) and adds it: a pack bundled as an uncompressed asset of an Android app (`noCompress`; the path is the APK, the offset and length its `AssetFileDescriptor`'s), or one inside any container that stores it uncompressed. The offset need not be aligned. Returns its layer ID, as `open_file`.

**Errors.** `ErrorCode::Io` if the file cannot be read or the range is not inside it, `ErrorCode::Corrupt` if the range is not a valid pack.

<Tabs groupId="lang" persist items={["Rust","Python","JavaScript","Swift","Java and Kotlin","Dart","Go","C","C++",".NET"]}>
<Tab value="Rust">
```rust
pub fn open_file_range(&self, path: &str, offset: u64, length: u64) -> Result<u32>
```
</Tab>

<Tab value="Python">
```python
def open_file_range(self, path: str, offset: int, length: int) -> int: ...
```
</Tab>

<Tab value="JavaScript">
```ts
openFileRange(path: string, offset: number, length: number): number;
```
</Tab>

<Tab value="Swift">
```swift
public func openFileRange(_ path: String, offset: UInt64, length: UInt64) throws(TeiGeodataError) -> UInt32
```
</Tab>

<Tab value="Java and Kotlin">
```java
public long openFileRange(String path, long offset, long length);
```
</Tab>

<Tab value="Dart">
```dart
int openFileRange(String path, int offset, int length);
```
</Tab>

<Tab value="Go">
```go

```
</Tab>

<Tab value="C">
```c
int32_t tg_engine_open_file_range(const tg_engine *handle, const uint8_t *path, size_t path_len, uint64_t offset, uint64_t length, uint32_t *out);
```
</Tab>

<Tab value="C++">

<Tab value=".NET">
```csharp

```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

## `remove` [#remove]

Removes the pack with this layer ID; false if no pack has it. Queries already running finish on the snapshot they started with; the pack's memory is released after them.

<Tabs groupId="lang" persist items={["Rust","Python","JavaScript","Swift","Java and Kotlin","Dart","Go","C","C++",".NET"]}>

## `get` [#get]

The place with this ID (`tgd:np/1`), or no row; a retired ID gives its survivor.

**Errors.** `ErrorCode::InvalidArgument` if `id` is not a place ID; `ErrorCode::Corrupt` if a section read is corrupt.

## `nearby` [#nearby]

The places nearest the place with this ID, not counting it, nearest first, at most `limit`, with `meters` and `bearing` (from each place to it); no rows for an unknown ID.

**Errors.** `ErrorCode::InvalidArgument` if `id` is not a place ID or `limit` exceeds `LIMIT_MAX`; `ErrorCode::Corrupt` if a section read is corrupt.

<Tabs groupId="lang" persist items={["Rust","Python","JavaScript","Swift","Java and Kotlin","Dart","Go","C","C++",".NET"]}>

## `search` [#search]

Places matching `query`, best first, at most `limit`; "Name, Parent" ranks a named parent first. The `score` column compares only within one query.

**Errors.** `ErrorCode::InvalidArgument` if `limit` exceeds `LIMIT_MAX`; `ErrorCode::Corrupt` if a section read is corrupt.

<Tabs groupId="lang" persist items={["Rust","Python","JavaScript","Swift","Java and Kotlin","Dart","Go","C","C++",".NET"]}>
<Tab value="Rust">
```rust
pub fn search(&self, query: &str, limit: u32) -> Result<Blob>
```
</Tab>

<Tab value="Python">
```python

```
</Tab>

<Tab value="JavaScript">

## `elevation_at` [#elevation_at]

The terrain height at the point, as one row: `meters` above the datum (bilinear between the DEM samples around it), `source` (the DEM product's key, null where the pack does not state it), `resolution_m` (the sample spacing north to south) and `datum` (`EGM2008`). No row where no pack has terrain there (the sea, outside every grid).

**Errors.** `ErrorCode::InvalidArgument` for a point off the globe; `ErrorCode::Corrupt` if a grid read is corrupt.

## `postal_lookup` [#postal_lookup]

The places postal code `code` names, one row per code and place, with the code's `postal`, `scheme`, `code_kind`, `valid_from` and `valid_to` columns. `scheme` names one scheme (`np`, `gb`); empty means every scheme whose rule accepts the input. The code may be typed with or without separators, in any case, or in another script's digits. Retired codes are returned too, with their validity.

**Errors.** `ErrorCode::Corrupt` if a section read is corrupt.

<Tabs groupId="lang" persist items={["Rust","Python","JavaScript","Swift","Java and Kotlin","Dart","Go","C","C++",".NET"]}>

## `tz_offset_at` [#tz_offset_at]

The UTC offset in force in `zone` (a tzdb name or link, `Asia/Kathmandu`) at `unix_seconds`, from the first layer whose zone rules hold the zone: one row with `seconds` east of UTC, `dst` (1 when tzdb counts it as daylight saving time) and `abbr` (`+0545`, `EDT`); no row where no layer holds the zone.

**Errors.** `ErrorCode::InvalidArgument` for an instant outside the years ±9,999; `ErrorCode::MissingComponent` if the rules that would hold the zone were not installed; `ErrorCode::Corrupt` if they are corrupt.

## `tz_local` [#tz_local]

The offsets a civil time may have in `zone`: one row with `kind` (`unique`, `gap` for a time a transition skips, `overlap` for one that happens twice), `before` and `after` in seconds east of UTC (the offsets before and after the transition: for an overlap the earlier and the later instant's; for a unique time both the same); no row where no layer holds the zone.

**Errors.** `ErrorCode::InvalidArgument` for a date that is not one of the years ±9,999 or a time out of range; otherwise as `Engine::tz_offset_at`.

<Tabs groupId="lang" persist items={["Rust","Python","JavaScript","Swift","Java and Kotlin","Dart","Go","C","C++",".NET"]}>

## `tz_rules_start` [#tz_rules_start]

The earliest instant `zone`'s rules cover, in Unix seconds: one `unix` row (its first transition, before which tzdb knows only local mean time; the year −9,999 for a zone that never changed); no row where no layer holds the zone.

**Errors.** As `Engine::tz_offset_at`.

## `boundary` [#boundary]

The outline of the place with this ID at level of detail `lod`, as one row: `id`, `lod` (the level read: 0 from a pack stored at full resolution only), `tolerance_m` (how far it may stray from the full-resolution outline), `vertices` and `geojson`, an RFC 7946 Feature ready for a map: a `Polygon` or `MultiPolygon` (outer rings counterclockwise, holes clockwise), or the place's `Point` when it has no outline. Level 0 is full resolution and 1 to `COARSEST_LOD` coarser; neighbours share their borders at every level. A whole country at level 0 can be megabytes: ask a coarser level to draw it small. No row for an unknown ID.

**Errors.** `ErrorCode::InvalidArgument` if `id` is not a place ID or `lod` exceeds `COARSEST_LOD`; `ErrorCode::MissingComponent` without `boundaries`; `ErrorCode::Corrupt` if a section read is corrupt.

<Tabs groupId="lang" persist items={["Rust","Python","JavaScript","Swift","Java and Kotlin","Dart","Go","C","C++",".NET"]}>

</Tab>

</Tab>

</Tab>


## `distance` [#distance]

The great-circle distance between the places with these IDs, as one row: `meters` on the mean Earth sphere and `bearing`, the initial bearing from `from` to `to` in degrees clockwise from north. No row when either ID is unknown. From a point, use `distance_m` and `bearing_deg` with the place's `lat` and `lon`.

**Errors.** `ErrorCode::InvalidArgument` if an ID is not a place ID; `ErrorCode::Corrupt` if a section read is corrupt.

## `fold` [#fold]

The search fold of a name: NFKD, lower case, optional accents dropped by script, spaces collapsed, recomposed to NFC. The same fold the forge and the search index use.

**Errors.** `ErrorCode::MissingComponent` in a build without `search`, whose Unicode tables it uses.

## `distance_m` [#distance_m]

Great-circle distance in metres between two points in degrees, by the haversine formula on the mean Earth sphere (error up to about 0.5% against the ellipsoid), as every query measures it, with the same digits on every platform.

**Errors.** `ErrorCode::InvalidArgument` if a latitude is outside -90..=90, a longitude outside -180..=180, or any value is not finite.

## `bearing_deg` [#bearing_deg]

The initial great-circle bearing from the first point to the second, in degrees clockwise from true north in `[0, 360)`; 0 for one point twice or from a pole. The same digits on every platform.

**Errors.** `ErrorCode::InvalidArgument` if a latitude is outside -90..=90, a longitude outside -180..=180, or any value is not finite.

# HTTP API (/docs/reference/http)

Every route answers `GET` with query parameters. A native route (`/v1/…`) answers `{"results": [...], "attribution": "..."}`, or `{"result": ..., "attribution": "..."}` for one value; each place has the fields of [a place](/docs/reference/mcp#places), because both servers map a place in one place. The Nominatim routes answer Nominatim's own format. How to run the server, with examples that ran: [HTTP server](/docs/servers/http).

Every native place route also takes:

| Parameter | Required | What |
|---|---|---|
| `format` |  | `json` (the default) or `geojson`: a FeatureCollection (RFC 7946) of the places. |

## Native routes [#native-routes]

### `/v1/search` [#v1search]

Places matching a name in any script or spelling, best first, each with its `score`. "Name, Parent" ranks places under a parent of that name first.

| Parameter | Required | What |
|---|---|---|
| `q` | yes | The name to find, such as `Pokhara`, `पोखरा` or `Pokhara, Kaski`. |
| `limit` |  | How many results: 10 by default, at most the server's bound (50). |
| `focus` |  | `lat,lon`: rank places near this point higher (30 points at the point, halving every `scale_km`). |
| `scale_km` |  | How far counts as near the focus, in km: 50 by default. Read only with `focus`. |
| `strict` |  | `1`: rank by how well the name matched before anything else. |

```http
GET /v1/search?q=Pokhara&limit=3&strict=1
GET /v1/search?q=Pokhara&focus=28.2,83.9&scale_km=20
```

### `/v1/get` [#v1get]

One place by its ID; a retired ID answers its survivor.

| Parameter | Required | What |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | yes | A place ID, such as `tgd:np/1xhb`. |
| `names` |  | `1`: add every name of the place, with its language and origin. |

```http
GET /v1/get?id=tgd:np/1xhb&names=1
```

### `/v1/lookup` [#v1lookup]

Places by ID, in the order asked; IDs not found are left out.

| Parameter | Required | What |
|---|---|---|
| `ids` | yes | Comma-separated place IDs, at most the server's `limit` bound. |

```http
GET /v1/lookup?ids=tgd:np/1xhb,tgd:np/1wmc
```

### `/v1/reverse` [#v1reverse]

The places nearest a point, nearest first, each with `meters`, `bearing` (degrees clockwise from north) and `inside` (its outline holds the point).

| Parameter | Required | What |
|---|---|---|
| `lat` | yes | Latitude, WGS84 degrees, -90 to 90. |
| `lon` | yes | Longitude, WGS84 degrees, -180 to 180. |
| `limit` |  | How many results: 10 by default, at most the server's bound (50). |
| `in_country` |  | `1`: only places in the country that holds the point. |

```http
GET /v1/reverse?lat=28.21&lon=83.99&limit=3&in_country=1
```

### `/v1/near` [#v1near]

The places nearest a place, nearest first, the place itself left out.

| Parameter | Required | What |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | yes | A place ID, such as `tgd:np/1xhb`. |
| `limit` |  | How many results: 10 by default, at most the server's bound (50). |
| `radius_m` |  | Only places within this many metres (at most 1,000,000). |

```http
GET /v1/near?id=tgd:np/1xhb&limit=5&radius_m=5000
```

### `/v1/admin` [#v1admin]

The admin units holding a point: the country first, then each finer level.

| Parameter | Required | What |
|---|---|---|
| `lat` | yes | Latitude, WGS84 degrees, -90 to 90. |
| `lon` | yes | Longitude, WGS84 degrees, -180 to 180. |

```http
GET /v1/admin?lat=27.7172&lon=85.324
```

### `/v1/hierarchy` [#v1hierarchy]

A place's ancestors: its parent first, up to the country.

| Parameter | Required | What |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | yes | A place ID, such as `tgd:np/1xhb`. |

```http
GET /v1/hierarchy?id=tgd:np/1xhb
```

### `/v1/children` [#v1children]

A place's children, by ID.

| Parameter | Required | What |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | yes | A place ID, such as `tgd:np/1xhb`. |
| `limit` |  | How many results: 10 by default, at most the server's bound (50). |

```http
GET /v1/children?id=tgd:np/1wmc&limit=20
```

### `/v1/tz` [#v1tz]

The timezone of a place or a point, with its UTC offset, abbreviation and daylight-saving flag at an instant.

| Parameter | Required | What |
|---|---|---|
| `id` |  | A place ID; or give `lat` and `lon`. |
| `lat` |  | Latitude, with `lon`, when no `id` is given. |
| `lon` |  | Longitude, with `lat`. |
| `t` |  | The instant, in Unix seconds: now by default. |

```http
GET /v1/tz?id=tgd:np/1xhb&t=1767225600
GET /v1/tz?lat=27.7172&lon=85.324
```

### `/v1/elevation` [#v1elevation]

The terrain height at a point in metres above EGM2008, with the grid's source and spacing. One value, under `result`.

| Parameter | Required | What |
|---|---|---|
| `lat` | yes | Latitude, WGS84 degrees, -90 to 90. |
| `lon` | yes | Longitude, WGS84 degrees, -180 to 180. |

```http
GET /v1/elevation?lat=27.9881&lon=86.925
```

### `/v1/distance` [#v1distance]

The great-circle distance in metres and the initial bearing between two points or places. One value, under `result`.

| Parameter | Required | What |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | yes | `lat,lon` or a place ID. |
| `to` | yes | `lat,lon` or a place ID. |

```http
GET /v1/distance?from=27.7172,85.324&to=tgd:np/1xhb
```

### `/v1/postal` [#v1postal]

The places a postal code names, codes starting with a prefix, or the codes at a point.

| Parameter | Required | What |
|---|---|---|
| `code` |  | A postal code, with or without separators, in any case or script's digits; or give `lat` and `lon`. |
| `scheme` |  | The scheme, when a country has more than one. |
| `prefix` |  | `1`: complete `code` as a prefix. |
| `limit` |  | How many results with `code`: 10 by default. |
| `lat` |  | Latitude, with `lon`, when no `code` is given. |
| `lon` |  | Longitude, with `lat`. |

```http
GET /v1/postal?code=44600&prefix=1&limit=5&scheme=np
GET /v1/postal?lat=27.7172&lon=85.324
```

### `/v1/boundary` [#v1boundary]

An admin unit's outline as a GeoJSON Feature, in any `format`.

| Parameter | Required | What |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | yes | A place ID, such as `tgd:np/1xhb`. |
| `lod` |  | The level of detail, 0 (finest, the default) to 6 (coarsest). |

```http
GET /v1/boundary?id=tgd:np/1wmc&lod=3
```

### `/v1/coverage` [#v1coverage]

The catalog's packs that cover a point, with their sizes: what to install for it. A server over a store only.

| Parameter | Required | What |
|---|---|---|
| `lat` | yes | Latitude, WGS84 degrees, -90 to 90. |
| `lon` | yes | Longitude, WGS84 degrees, -180 to 180. |
| `radius_m` |  | Also the packs within this many metres. |

```http
GET /v1/coverage?lat=25.2048&lon=55.2708&radius_m=10000
```

## Nominatim routes [#nominatim-routes]

The parameters and fields of Nominatim that its clients use; what teigeodata cannot fill is left out, never faked. IDs are teigeodata's.

### `/search` [#search]

Nominatim's search: a JSON array of Nominatim places.

| Parameter | Required | What |
|---|---|---|
| `q` |  | Free-form text; or the structured fields below. |
| `amenity` |  | Structured search: joined with the other fields, most specific first. |
| `street` |  | Structured search. |
| `city` |  | Structured search. |
| `county` |  | Structured search. |
| `state` |  | Structured search. |
| `country` |  | Structured search. |
| `postalcode` |  | Structured search. |
| `limit` |  | How many results: 10 by default, at most 40. |
| `countrycodes` |  | Comma-separated ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes to keep. |
| `viewbox` |  | `x1,y1,x2,y2` (longitude first): rank places in the box higher. |
| `bounded` |  | `1`: only places in `viewbox`. |
| `addressdetails` |  | `1`: add each place's `address`. |
| `format` |  | `json` (the default), `jsonv2` (the same) or `geojson`. |
| `json_callback` |  | Refused: JSONP is not supported; call with CORS. |

```http
GET /search?q=Pokhara&limit=3&countrycodes=np&viewbox=83.8,28.1,84.1,28.3&bounded=1&addressdetails=1&format=jsonv2
GET /search?city=Pokhara&country=Nepal
```

### `/reverse` [#reverse]

Nominatim's reverse: the place at a point at a zoom's depth, or `{"error": "Unable to geocode"}`.

| Parameter | Required | What |
|---|---|---|
| `lat` | yes | Latitude, WGS84 degrees, -90 to 90. |
| `lon` | yes | Longitude, WGS84 degrees, -180 to 180. |
| `zoom` |  | How deep: 3 a country, 5 to 7 a first-level unit, 8 and 9 the next, 10 to 18 the nearest place within reach; 18 by default. |
| `addressdetails` |  | `0` leaves out `address` (on by default). |
| `format` |  | `json` (the default), `jsonv2` (the same) or `geojson`. |
| `json_callback` |  | Refused: JSONP is not supported. |

```http
GET /reverse?lat=28.21&lon=83.99&zoom=10&addressdetails=0&format=geojson
```

### `/lookup` [#lookup]

Nominatim's lookup: places by ID, as a JSON array.

| Parameter | Required | What |
|---|---|---|
| `osm_ids` | yes | Comma-separated teigeodata IDs, at most 50; an OSM reference such as `N123` is left out as not found. |
| `addressdetails` |  | `1`: add each place's `address`. |
| `format` |  | `json` (the default), `jsonv2` (the same) or `geojson`. |
| `json_callback` |  | Refused: JSONP is not supported. |

```http
GET /lookup?osm_ids=tgd:np/1xhb,N123&addressdetails=1
```

## Other routes [#other-routes]

| Route | What |
|---|---|
| `/packs` | The packs served: each one's release, components, places and attribution. |
| `/health` | `{"status": "ok", "layers": n}` while the server answers. |
| `/mcp` | The [MCP server](/docs/reference/mcp), over Streamable HTTP. |

## Errors [#errors]

A failure answers `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}}` with the code's HTTP status; a Nominatim route puts the status in `code`. Codes are stable: one may be added, none changes its meaning.

| Code | Status | Meaning |
|---|--:|---|
| `invalid_argument` | 400 | A parameter does not parse or has no meaning (a bad ID, a latitude past 90°). |
| `out_of_bounds` | 400 | A parameter is past a server bound: too long a text, too large a `limit`, too far a radius. A query string that is too long answers 414. |
| `not_found` | 404 | The place is not in the packs, or there is no such route. |
| `missing_component` | 501 | The packs served lack the component that answers this. |
| `unauthenticated` | 401 | The caller must say who they are: only a deployment that adds keys answers it. |
| `forbidden` | 403 | The caller may not ask this: only a deployment that adds rules answers it. |
| `rate_limited` | 429 | Too much, too fast: only a deployment that adds limits answers it. |
| `unavailable` | 503 | The server cannot answer now (the request took longer than its timeout); asking again later may work. |
| `internal` | 500 | The server failed; never the client's fault. |

# Reference (/docs/reference)

The API is defined once, in Rust (`teigeodata-api`), and every binding is generated from that
definition, so this reference is generated from it too: each entry gives the documentation
written in the API and the declaration each language's binding is written with. It holds
33 engine methods, 22
store and job methods and 8 functions.

Names follow each language's style; the entries use the Rust ones:

| Rust, Python, C++ | JavaScript, Swift, Java, Kotlin, Dart | Go, .NET | C |
|---|---|---|---|
| `search_with` | `searchWith` | `SearchWith` | `tg_engine_search_with` |
| `admin_at` | `adminAt` | `AdminAt` | `tg_engine_admin_at` |
| `tz_offset_at` | `tzOffsetAt` | `TzOffsetAt` | `tg_engine_tz_offset_at` |

Queries return a [result blob](/docs/concepts/results) read with each language's `Reader`.
The servers have their own reference: every route of the [HTTP API](/docs/reference/http)
and every tool of the [MCP server](/docs/reference/mcp), generated from the servers' own
definitions.

## Engine [#engine]

The [Engine page](/docs/reference/engine) has each method's declaration in every language.

| Name | What |
|---|---|
| [`new`](/docs/reference/engine#new) | An engine with no packs. |
| [`open_file`](/docs/reference/engine#open_file) | Opens the pack at `path` (memory-mapped) and adds it. |
| [`open_file_with`](/docs/reference/engine#open_file_with) | Opens the pack at `path` with these options and adds it. |
| [`open_file_range`](/docs/reference/engine#open_file_range) | Opens the pack stored whole in `length` bytes at `offset` of the file at `path` (memory-mapped) and adds it: a pack bundled as an uncompressed asset of an Android app (`noCompress`; the path is the APK, the offset and length its `AssetFileDescriptor`'s), or one inside any container that stores it uncompressed. |
| [`open_file_range_with`](/docs/reference/engine#open_file_range_with) | As `open_file_range`, with these options. |
| [`open_bytes`](/docs/reference/engine#open_bytes) | Adds a pack from its bytes (copied). |
| [`open_bytes_with`](/docs/reference/engine#open_bytes_with) | Adds a pack from its bytes (copied) with these options. |
| [`remove`](/docs/reference/engine#remove) | Removes the pack with this layer ID; false if no pack has it. |
| [`layers`](/docs/reference/engine#layers) | The number of packs. |
| [`get`](/docs/reference/engine#get) | The place with this ID (`tgd:np/1`), or no row; a retired ID gives its survivor. |
| [`parent`](/docs/reference/engine#parent) | The place's parent as the packs answer for it (one row), or no row for a root or an unknown ID. |
| [`ancestors`](/docs/reference/engine#ancestors) | The place's ancestors, parent first up to the country; no rows for a root or an unknown ID. |
| [`children`](/docs/reference/engine#children) | The place's children, by ID; no rows for a leaf or an unknown ID. |
| [`nearby`](/docs/reference/engine#nearby) | The places nearest the place with this ID, not counting it, nearest first, at most `limit`, with `meters` and `bearing` (from each place to it); no rows for an unknown ID. |
| [`search`](/docs/reference/engine#search) | Places matching `query`, best first, at most `limit`; "Name, Parent" ranks a named parent first. |
| [`search_with`](/docs/reference/engine#search_with) | `search` ranked by `options`: near a focus point, or in strict match order. |
| [`reverse`](/docs/reference/engine#reverse) | The places nearest the point, nearest first, at most `limit`, with `meters` and `bearing` (degrees clockwise from north, from each place to the point). |
| [`within_radius`](/docs/reference/engine#within_radius) | The places within `radius_m` metres of the point (great-circle), nearest first, at most `limit`, with `meters` and `bearing` (from each place to the point). |
| [`admin_at`](/docs/reference/engine#admin_at) | The admin units holding the point, country first. |
| [`elevation_at`](/docs/reference/engine#elevation_at) | The terrain height at the point, as one row: `meters` above the datum (bilinear between the DEM samples around it), `source` (the DEM product's key, null where the pack does not state it), `resolution_m` (the sample spacing north to south) and `datum` (`EGM2008`). |
| [`postal_lookup`](/docs/reference/engine#postal_lookup) | The places postal code `code` names, one row per code and place, with the code's `postal`, `scheme`, `code_kind`, `valid_from` and `valid_to` columns. |
| [`postal_prefix`](/docs/reference/engine#postal_prefix) | Up to `limit` postal codes starting with `prefix`, with their places (autocomplete), in code order per scheme; `scheme` as in `postal_lookup`. |
| [`postal_codes_of`](/docs/reference/engine#postal_codes_of) | The postal codes of the place with this ID; no rows for an unknown ID. |
| [`postal_at`](/docs/reference/engine#postal_at) | The postal codes of the point: those of the deepest admin unit holding it that an admin-aligned scheme gives codes to, with its parts (a ward's code; the point is in one of them). |
| [`tz_at`](/docs/reference/engine#tz_at) | The time-zone area holding the point (one row; its `tz` column is the IANA zone), or no row where no pack answers. |
| [`tz_offset_at`](/docs/reference/engine#tz_offset_at) | The UTC offset in force in `zone` (a tzdb name or link, `Asia/Kathmandu`) at `unix_seconds`, from the first layer whose zone rules hold the zone: one row with `seconds` east of UTC, `dst` (1 when tzdb counts it as daylight saving time) and `abbr` (`+0545`, `EDT`); no row where no layer holds the zone. |
| [`tz_local`](/docs/reference/engine#tz_local) | The offsets a civil time may have in `zone`: one row with `kind` (`unique`, `gap` for a time a transition skips, `overlap` for one that happens twice), `before` and `after` in seconds east of UTC (the offsets before and after the transition: for an overlap the earlier and the later instant's; for a unique time both the same); no row where no layer holds the zone. |
| [`tz_zones`](/docs/reference/engine#tz_zones) | Every zone name (tzdb names and links) the layers' zone rules hold, in byte order: one `zone` column. |
| [`tz_rules_start`](/docs/reference/engine#tz_rules_start) | The earliest instant `zone`'s rules cover, in Unix seconds: one `unix` row (its first transition, before which tzdb knows only local mean time; the year −9,999 for a zone that never changed); no row where no layer holds the zone. |
| [`tz_version`](/docs/reference/engine#tz_version) | The tzdb release (`2026f`) of the first layer with zone rules; empty without rules. |
| [`by_iso`](/docs/reference/engine#by_iso) | The place whose ISO 3166 code is `code` (`NP`, `NP-P3`, either case), or no row. |
| [`boundary`](/docs/reference/engine#boundary) | The outline of the place with this ID at level of detail `lod`, as one row: `id`, `lod` (the level read: 0 from a pack stored at full resolution only), `tolerance_m` (how far it may stray from the full-resolution outline), `vertices` and `geojson`, an RFC 7946 Feature ready for a map: a `Polygon` or `MultiPolygon` (outer rings counterclockwise, holes clockwise), or the place's `Point` when it has no outline. |
| [`distance`](/docs/reference/engine#distance) | The great-circle distance between the places with these IDs, as one row: `meters` on the mean Earth sphere and `bearing`, the initial bearing from `from` to `to` in degrees clockwise from north. |

## Store [#store]

The [Store page](/docs/reference/store#store) has each method's declaration in every language.

| Name | What |
|---|---|
| [`create`](/docs/reference/store#create) | Sets up a store at `root` and opens it: the metadata mirrors `repo` and asset mirrors `assets` (comma-separated URLs), and `trusted_root`, the catalog's root metadata, which becomes its trust anchor once it verifies by itself. |
| [`open`](/docs/reference/store#open) | Opens the store at `root`, finishing or undoing an install a crash cut short. |
| [`damaged`](/docs/reference/store#damaged) | The packs found damaged when the store was opened, comma-separated; empty when none. |
| [`catalog`](/docs/reference/store#catalog) | The verified catalog as stored, one row per pack, with its state against the store. |
| [`status`](/docs/reference/store#status) | Each installed pack and its health, from a full check of every byte when `deep`. |
| [`pin`](/docs/reference/store#pin) | Pins the pack (kept when room is made), or unpins it. |
| [`remove`](/docs/reference/store#remove) | Removes the packs and the dependencies nothing else needs; returns what was removed. |
| [`find`](/docs/reference/store#find) | The places named `query` in `engine` (one over a world pack the app ships, the installed packs, or both), best first, each with the catalog's packs that cover it: what to install for "Dubai". |
| [`locate`](/docs/reference/store#locate) | The countries within `radius_m` metres of a point in `engine`, each with the catalog's packs that cover the point: what to install for where the user stands. |
| [`engine`](/docs/reference/store#engine) | An engine over the installed packs, each opened with the components and languages installed. |
| [`refresh`](/docs/reference/store#refresh) | Refreshes the catalog for the countries (comma-separated ISO codes) and every country installed. |
| [`install`](/docs/reference/store#install) | Installs the packs with `options`, dependencies first, refreshing the catalog for their countries. |
| [`install_pass`](/docs/reference/store#install_pass) | One pass of an install whose bytes a platform's own download service fetches, for downloads that must go on while the app is suspended. |
| [`update`](/docs/reference/store#update) | Updates the packs (every installed one when empty) to the catalog's releases, keeping the components and languages installed. |
| [`repair`](/docs/reference/store#repair) | Checks the pack in full and, unless it is whole, fetches what it lacks. |

## Job [#job]

A job's methods are on the [Store page](/docs/reference/store#job).

| Name | What |
|---|---|
| [`wait_progress`](/docs/reference/store#wait_progress) | Waits until the progress moves past `seq` (from `seq`), the job ends, or `timeout_ms` passes; returns the sequence then. |
| [`seq`](/docs/reference/store#seq) | The progress's sequence number: it moves on with every change. |
| [`done_bytes`](/docs/reference/store#done_bytes) | Bytes received so far. |
| [`total_bytes`](/docs/reference/store#total_bytes) | Bytes expected, from the catalog's sizes: never below the bytes received, and equal to them once the job ends. |
| [`is_ended`](/docs/reference/store#is_ended) | Whether the job has ended (done, failed or cancelled); its result is then ready. |
| [`cancel`](/docs/reference/store#cancel) | Asks the job to stop at its next request or chunk; it then fails with `ErrorCode::Cancelled` and leaves the store as it was. |
| [`result`](/docs/reference/store#result) | The job's result, waiting for it to end. |

## Functions [#functions]

The [functions page](/docs/reference/functions) has each declaration in every language.

| Name | What |
|---|---|
| [`version`](/docs/reference/functions#version) | The library version, from its package metadata. |
| [`components`](/docs/reference/functions#components) | The components this build answers, in table order, comma-separated (`point, elevation, admin`). |
| [`noop`](/docs/reference/functions#noop) | Does nothing. |
| [`fold`](/docs/reference/functions#fold) | The search fold of a name: NFKD, lower case, optional accents dropped by script, spaces collapsed, recomposed to NFC. |
| [`sample_rows`](/docs/reference/functions#sample_rows) | Builds `rows` deterministic sample places as a blob with the columns `id` (`u32`), `lat` and `lon` (`f64`, degrees), `elevation` (`f32`, metres) and `name` (UTF-8). |
| [`progress`](/docs/reference/functions#progress) | Calls `on_step` once per step with the step number, from 1 to `steps`, on the calling thread, and returns the number of steps run. |
| [`distance_m`](/docs/reference/functions#distance_m) | Great-circle distance in metres between two points in degrees, by the haversine formula on the mean Earth sphere (error up to about 0.5% against the ellipsoid), as every query measures it, with the same digits on every platform. |
| [`bearing_deg`](/docs/reference/functions#bearing_deg) | The initial great-circle bearing from the first point to the second, in degrees clockwise from true north in `[0, 360)`; 0 for one point twice or from a pole. |

## Types, constants and errors [#types-constants-and-errors]

Every record, enum, constant and error code is on the [types page](/docs/reference/types):

[`SearchOptions`](/docs/reference/types#searchoptions), [`OpenOptions`](/docs/reference/types#openoptions), [`InstallOptions`](/docs/reference/types#installoptions);
[`Verify`](/docs/reference/types#verify), [`Load`](/docs/reference/types#load);
[constants](/docs/reference/types#constants) and [error codes](/docs/reference/types#errors).

# MCP tools (/docs/reference/mcp)

What `tools/list` and `resources/templates/list` give, with the bounds of a server's default limits. Every answer is structured content that its tool's output schema accepts, the same object as text, with the attribution under `_meta` too. How to run the server and connect a client: [MCP server](/docs/servers/mcp).

The server's instructions to a client:

> Offline place data. Find places by name with `search`, by coordinates with `reverse` and `admin_at`, around a place with `nearby`; climb with `hierarchy` and descend with `children`. Places are named by IDs such as tgd:np/1xhb: pass them to `get_place`, `lookup`, `nearby`, `timezone` or read teigeodata://place/\{id\}. Coordinates are WGS84 degrees, distances metres, heights metres above EGM2008. A long answer has a `next_cursor`: call the same tool with only `cursor` for the next page. Show the `attribution` of an answer wherever its data is shown: the licences require it.

## Tools [#tools]

| Tool | What |
|---|---|
| [`search`](#search) | Search places by name |
| [`reverse`](#reverse) | Places nearest a point |
| [`nearby`](#nearby) | Places near a place |
| [`get_place`](#get_place) | A place by ID |
| [`lookup`](#lookup) | Places by IDs |
| [`admin_at`](#admin_at) | Admin units at a point |
| [`hierarchy`](#hierarchy) | Ancestors of a place |
| [`children`](#children) | Children of a place |
| [`timezone`](#timezone) | Timezone |
| [`elevation`](#elevation) | Terrain height |
| [`postal`](#postal) | Postal codes |
| [`boundary`](#boundary) | Outline of a place |
| [`distance`](#distance) | Distance and bearing |
| [`packs`](#packs) | Installed packs |
| [`coverage`](#coverage) | Packs for a point |
| [`install`](#install) | Install packs |
| [`install_status`](#install_status) | How an install goes |

### `search` [#search]

**Search places by name.** Places matching a name, best first. "Name, Parent" ranks places under a parent of that name first. `focus` ranks places near a point higher (scale_km: how far counts as near, default 50). `strict` ranks by how well the name matched (exact, then loose, prefix, one edit) before importance and nearness.

Hints: read-only, idempotent.

| Argument | Type | Required | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string | yes | The name, in any script, such as Pokhara or पोखरा. 1 to 256 bytes. |
| `cursor` | string |  | The `next_cursor` of the previous page; the other arguments are then taken from it. |
| `focus` | object |  |  |
| `focus.lat` | number | yes | Latitude, WGS84 degrees. -90 to 90. |
| `focus.lon` | number | yes | Longitude, WGS84 degrees. -180 to 180. |
| `focus.scale_km` | number |  | Over 0; default `50`. |
| `limit` | integer |  | How many results, the page's size. 0 to 50; default `10`. |
| `strict` | boolean |  | Rank by match quality first. Default `false`. |

Answers [places](#places), a page at a time.

### `reverse` [#reverse]

**Places nearest a point.** The places nearest a point, nearest first, each with its distance in metres, its bearing, and whether its outline holds the point. `in_country`: only places in the country holding the point.

Hints: read-only, idempotent.

| Argument | Type | Required | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lat` | number | yes | Latitude, WGS84 degrees. -90 to 90. |
| `lon` | number | yes | Longitude, WGS84 degrees. -180 to 180. |
| `cursor` | string |  | The `next_cursor` of the previous page; the other arguments are then taken from it. |
| `in_country` | boolean |  | Default `false`. |
| `limit` | integer |  | How many results, the page's size. 0 to 50; default `10`. |

Answers [places](#places), a page at a time.

### `nearby` [#nearby]

**Places near a place.** The places nearest a place, nearest first, the place itself left out; within `radius_m` metres when given.

Hints: read-only, idempotent.

| Argument | Type | Required | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | A place ID from an earlier answer, such as tgd:np/1xhb. 1 to 256 bytes. |
| `cursor` | string |  | The `next_cursor` of the previous page; the other arguments are then taken from it. |
| `limit` | integer |  | How many results, the page's size. 0 to 50; default `10`. |
| `radius_m` | number |  | Metres. 0 to 1000000.0. |

Answers [places](#places), a page at a time.

### `get_place` [#get_place]

**A place by ID.** One place by its ID; `names`: every name it has, with language and origin. A retired ID answers its survivor.

Hints: read-only, idempotent.

| Argument | Type | Required | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | A place ID from an earlier answer, such as tgd:np/1xhb. 1 to 256 bytes. |
| `names` | boolean |  | Default `false`. |

Answers [places](#places), a page at a time.

### `lookup` [#lookup]

**Places by IDs.** Places by ID, in the order asked; IDs not found are left out.

Hints: read-only, idempotent.

| Argument | Type | Required | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ids` | array of string | yes | 1 to 50 items. |

Answers [places](#places), a page at a time.

### `admin_at` [#admin_at]

**Admin units at a point.** The admin units holding a point, the country first, then each finer level.

Hints: read-only, idempotent.

| Argument | Type | Required | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lat` | number | yes | Latitude, WGS84 degrees. -90 to 90. |
| `lon` | number | yes | Longitude, WGS84 degrees. -180 to 180. |

Answers [places](#places), a page at a time.

### `hierarchy` [#hierarchy]

**Ancestors of a place.** A place's ancestors: its parent first, then the parent's, up to the country.

Hints: read-only, idempotent.

| Argument | Type | Required | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | A place ID from an earlier answer, such as tgd:np/1xhb. 1 to 256 bytes. |

Answers [places](#places), a page at a time.

### `children` [#children]

**Children of a place.** The places whose parent is a place, such as a country's provinces or a district's municipalities.

Hints: read-only, idempotent.

| Argument | Type | Required | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | A place ID from an earlier answer, such as tgd:np/1xhb. 1 to 256 bytes. |
| `cursor` | string |  | The `next_cursor` of the previous page; the other arguments are then taken from it. |
| `limit` | integer |  | How many results, the page's size. 0 to 50; default `10`. |

Answers [places](#places), a page at a time.

### `timezone` [#timezone]

**Timezone.** The IANA timezone of a place (`id`) or at a point (`lat`, `lon`), with its UTC offset, abbreviation and DST at instant `t` (Unix seconds, default now).

Hints: read-only, idempotent.

| Argument | Type | Required | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string |  | A place ID from an earlier answer, such as tgd:np/1xhb. 1 to 256 bytes. |
| `lat` | number |  | Latitude, WGS84 degrees. -90 to 90. |
| `lon` | number |  | Longitude, WGS84 degrees. -180 to 180. |
| `t` | integer |  | Unix seconds. |

Answers [places](#places), a page at a time.

### `elevation` [#elevation]

**Terrain height.** The terrain height at a point, metres above the EGM2008 geoid, from the packs' elevation model; null where there is none.

Hints: read-only, idempotent.

| Argument | Type | Required | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lat` | number | yes | Latitude, WGS84 degrees. -90 to 90. |
| `lon` | number | yes | Longitude, WGS84 degrees. -180 to 180. |

Answers:

| Field | Type | What |
|---|---|---|
| `attribution` | string or null |  |
| `result` | object |  |
| `result.datum` | string |  |
| `result.elevation_m` | number or null |  |
| `result.lat` | number |  |
| `result.lon` | number |  |
| `result.resolution_m` | number |  |
| `result.source` | string or null |  |

### `postal` [#postal]

**Postal codes.** Postal codes: a code to its places (`code`, optionally its `scheme` such as NP or IN-PIN), codes starting with `code` (`prefix`), or the codes at a point (`lat`, `lon`).

Hints: read-only, idempotent.

| Argument | Type | Required | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| `code` | string |  | 1 to 256 bytes. |
| `lat` | number |  | Latitude, WGS84 degrees. -90 to 90. |
| `limit` | integer |  | How many results, the page's size. 0 to 50; default `10`. |
| `lon` | number |  | Longitude, WGS84 degrees. -180 to 180. |
| `prefix` | boolean |  | Default `false`. |
| `scheme` | string |  | At most 256 bytes. |

Answers:

| Field | Type | What |
|---|---|---|
| `attribution` | string or null |  |
| `results` | array of object |  |
| `results[].admin_level` | integer |  |
| `results[].code` | string |  |
| `results[].id` | string |  |
| `results[].kind` | string |  |
| `results[].name` | string or null |  |
| `results[].replaced` | boolean |  |
| `results[].scheme` | string |  |
| `results[].valid_from` | integer or null |  |
| `results[].valid_to` | integer or null |  |

### `boundary` [#boundary]

**Outline of a place.** What a place's outline is: its level of detail (0 finest to 6 coarsest; the finest within the vertex bound when `lod` is not given), tolerance in metres, vertices, parts, holes and bounding box, and the `uri` of the outline itself as a GeoJSON resource, to read when it is drawn. A place with no outline answers `outlined: false`.

Hints: read-only, idempotent.

| Argument | Type | Required | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | A place ID from an earlier answer, such as tgd:np/1xhb. 1 to 256 bytes. |
| `lod` | integer |  | 0 to 6. |

Answers:

| Field | Type | What |
|---|---|---|
| `attribution` | string or null |  |
| `result` | object |  |
| `result.bbox` | array or null | West, south, east, north. 4 to 4 items. |
| `result.id` | string |  |
| `result.lod` | integer |  |
| `result.name` | string or null |  |
| `result.outlined` | boolean |  |
| `result.uri` | string |  |
| `result.vertices` | integer |  |
| `result.holes` | integer |  |
| `result.parts` | integer |  |
| `result.tolerance_m` | number |  |

### `distance` [#distance]

**Distance and bearing.** The great-circle distance in metres and initial bearing between two ends, each a place ID or a point as `lat,lon`.

Hints: read-only, idempotent.

| Argument | Type | Required | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| `from` | string | yes | A place ID such as tgd:np/1xhb, or a point such as 27.7172,85.324. 1 to 256 bytes. |
| `to` | string | yes | A place ID, or a point as `lat,lon`. 1 to 256 bytes. |

Answers:

| Field | Type | What |
|---|---|---|
| `attribution` | string or null |  |
| `result` | object |  |
| `result.bearing` | number | Degrees clockwise from north. |
| `result.from` | object |  |
| `result.from.id` | string or null |  |
| `result.from.lat` | number |  |
| `result.from.lon` | number |  |
| `result.meters` | number |  |
| `result.to` | object |  |
| `result.to.id` | string or null |  |
| `result.to.lat` | number |  |
| `result.to.lon` | number |  |

### `packs` [#packs]

**Installed packs.** The packs served: address, component, release, places, installed components and attribution.

Hints: read-only, idempotent.

No arguments.

Answers:

| Field | Type | What |
|---|---|---|
| `packs` | array of object |  |
| `packs[].address` | string |  |
| `packs[].attribution` | string or null |  |
| `packs[].component` | string |  |
| `packs[].components` | array of string |  |
| `packs[].places` | integer |  |
| `packs[].release` | string |  |

### `coverage` [#coverage]

**Packs for a point.** The countries at a point or within `radius_m` metres of it, each with the catalog's packs that could hold the point: path, release, download and disk bytes, components, parts, licence and state (installed, update or available). From the store's verified catalog, offline.

Listed only by a server over a store (`--store`).

Hints: read-only, idempotent.

| Argument | Type | Required | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lat` | number | yes | Latitude, WGS84 degrees. -90 to 90. |
| `lon` | number | yes | Longitude, WGS84 degrees. -180 to 180. |
| `radius_m` | integer |  | Metres; default 3,000. 0 to 1000000.0. |

Answers:

| Field | Type | What |
|---|---|---|
| `attribution` | string or null |  |
| `results` | array of object |  |
| `results[].countries` | array of string |  |
| `results[].id` | string |  |
| `results[].lat` | number |  |
| `results[].lon` | number |  |
| `results[].name` | string or null |  |
| `results[].packs` | array of object |  |
| `results[].packs[].components` | array of string |  |
| `results[].packs[].disk` | integer |  |
| `results[].packs[].download` | integer |  |
| `results[].packs[].path` | string |  |
| `results[].packs[].release` | string |  |
| `results[].packs[].state` | string | One of `installed`, `update`, `available`. |
| `results[].packs[].licence` | string |  |
| `results[].packs[].parts` | array of object |  |

### `install` [#install]

**Install packs.** Downloads packs from the catalog into the store, verified, and serves them: `packs` as catalog paths or addresses (np, np.places, ae-du), `components` (every one when none). The person confirms the download's size when the client can ask; otherwise the call is refused past `max_bytes` (default 100 MB), naming the size. Answers a task, or a `handle` for `install_status`.

Listed only by a server over a store that allows installs (`--allow-install`).

Hints: changes the store, idempotent, reaches the network.

| Argument | Type | Required | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| `packs` | array of string | yes | 1 to 16 items. |
| `components` | array of string |  |  |
| `max_bytes` | integer |  | The most this call may download without the person's confirmation; default 100,000,000. At least 0. |

Answers:

| Field | Type | What |
|---|---|---|
| `attribution` | null |  |
| `result` | object |  |
| `result.status` | string | One of `working`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `declined`. |
| `result.download` | integer |  |
| `result.error` | object or null |  |
| `result.handle` | string |  |
| `result.message` | string |  |
| `result.packs` | array of string |  |
| `result.result` | object or null |  |

### `install_status` [#install_status]

**How an install goes.** Where the install of a `handle` (from `install`) is: working, completed, failed or cancelled, with its message and, once ended, what it installed or why it failed. Ask about once a second.

Listed only by a server over a store that allows installs (`--allow-install`).

Hints: read-only, idempotent.

| Argument | Type | Required | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| `handle` | string | yes | 32 to 32 bytes. |

Answers:

| Field | Type | What |
|---|---|---|
| `attribution` | null |  |
| `result` | object |  |
| `result.status` | string | One of `working`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `declined`. |
| `result.download` | integer |  |
| `result.error` | object or null |  |
| `result.handle` | string |  |
| `result.message` | string |  |
| `result.packs` | array of string |  |
| `result.result` | object or null |  |

## Places [#places]

The answer of every place tool: a page of `results`, the `next_cursor` of the next page when there is one, and the `attribution` of the packs that answered. A field a place lacks is left out or null.

| Field | Type | What |
|---|---|---|
| `attribution` | string or null | The credits of the packs that answered: show them wherever the data is shown. |
| `results` | array of object |  |
| `results[].admin_level` | integer | 1 for a country's first-level units, deeper units after; 0 for a country and for a place that is not an admin unit. |
| `results[].elevation` | integer or null | Metres above EGM2008. |
| `results[].id` | string | Its stable ID, such as tgd:np/1xhb. |
| `results[].kind` | string or null | Its kind, such as settlement or admin. |
| `results[].name` | string or null | Its canonical name. |
| `results[].parent` | string or null | Its parent's ID; null for a root. |
| `results[].timezone` | string or null | Its IANA timezone, such as Asia/Kathmandu. |
| `results[].bearing` | number | Degrees clockwise from north, from the place to the point asked about. |
| `results[].elevation_source` | string | Where the height came from: surveyed or model, when stated. |
| `results[].inside` | boolean | Whether the point asked about is inside the place's outline (reverse). |
| `results[].is_dst` | boolean | Whether daylight saving time is in force at that instant. |
| `results[].iso_code` | string | Its ISO 3166 code, for a country or unit that has one. |
| `results[].lat` | number | Latitude, WGS84 degrees. |
| `results[].lon` | number | Longitude, WGS84 degrees. |
| `results[].meters` | number | Distance from the point or place asked about, metres. |
| `results[].names` | array of object | Every name, canonical first (get_place with names). |
| `results[].names[].machine` | boolean | Made by a machine (a romanisation, a transliteration or a donor label): an app may show it differently. |
| `results[].names[].origin` | string | Where the name came from. |
| `results[].names[].text` | string |  |
| `results[].names[].kind` | string | The name's type. |
| `results[].names[].lang` | string | A BCP 47 tag, such as ne-Deva. |
| `results[].population` | integer | Its number of people, when known. |
| `results[].population_kind` | string | Where the number came from: stated (a source's count) or modelled (a population grid over an admin unit). |
| `results[].score` | integer | Its search score, comparable only within one query. |
| `results[].tz_abbr` | string | The zone's abbreviation at that instant. |
| `results[].utc_offset` | string | The UTC offset at the instant asked, such as +05:45 (timezone). |
| `next_cursor` | string | Pass as `cursor` to the same tool for the next page; absent on the last. |

## Resources [#resources]

| URI template | What | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `teigeodata://place/{id}` | A place: A place by its ID (tgd:np/1xhb), with every name, as a GeoJSON feature | `application/geo+json` |
| `teigeodata://boundary/{id}{?lod}` | A place's outline: A place's outline as a GeoJSON feature, simplified to level of detail `lod` (0 finest to 6 coarsest) | `application/geo+json` |
| `teigeodata://dataset/{address}/{component}` | A pack: A pack (np/places): its release, places, installed components and attribution | `application/json` |

## Errors [#errors]

A tool that fails answers a tool error (`isError`) whose text is `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}}`, with the codes of the [HTTP API](/docs/reference/http#errors).

# Store and Job (/docs/reference/store)

<Callout title="Native builds only">
The store is part of the `store` feature: in every native library, and left out of
the WebAssembly build, where the browser's own cache keeps packs. The signed catalog it installs
from goes live with the first catalog release; see [the store](/docs/concepts/store).
</Callout>

## Store [#store]

A store of installed packs in one directory: its signed catalog, its packs and their journal, shared by every language and the command line (research note store-api). Long work runs as a `Job` on a thread of its own; one store runs its jobs one at a time, and its other calls wait for the job running.

Packs are named as catalog paths (`np.places.tgd`) or short (`np`, `np.dem`), several comma-separated. Results are blobs:
- `catalog`: `path`, `release`, `download`, `disk`, `components`, `licence`, `state` (`available`, `installed` or `update`);
- `status`: `path`, `release`, `bytes`, `pinned`, `asked`, `health` (`good`, `length`, `head`, `footer` or `sections`), `components`;
- an install or update: `path`, `release`, `fetched`, `reused`, `kept`, `changed`;
- a refresh: `timestamp`, `files`, `bytes`; a repair: `path`, `health`, `fetched`; `remove`: `path`, `release`;
- `find` and `locate`: one row per place and pack that covers it: `id`, `name`, `lat`, `lon`, `countries`, then the pack's `pack`, `release`, `download`, `disk` and `state`, null for a place no pack in the catalog covers.

### `create` [#create]

Sets up a store at `root` and opens it: the metadata mirrors `repo` and asset mirrors `assets` (comma-separated URLs), and `trusted_root`, the catalog's root metadata, which becomes its trust anchor once it verifies by itself. A store set up before is set up again with these.

**Errors.** `ErrorCode::Refused` if the root does not verify or the store cannot be written.

**Blocks.** While a job of this store runs, and on the disk: call it off a UI thread, or use the language's asynchronous form.

<Tabs groupId="lang" persist items={["Rust","Python","JavaScript","Swift","Java and Kotlin","Dart","Go","C","C++",".NET"]}>
<Tab value="Rust">
```rust
pub fn create(root: &str, repo: &str, assets: &str, trusted_root: &[u8]) -> Result<Self>
```
</Tab>

<Tab value="Python">
```python
def create(root: str, repo: str, assets: str, trusted_root: bytes) -> Store: ...
```
</Tab>

<Tab value="JavaScript">
```ts

```
</Tab>

<Tab value="Swift">
```swift

```
</Tab>

<Tab value="Java and Kotlin">
```java

```
</Tab>

<Tab value="Dart">
```dart

```
</Tab>

</Tab>

</Tab>

<Tab value="C++">
```cpp

```
</Tab>

<Tab value=".NET">
```csharp

```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

### `open` [#open]

Opens the store at `root`, finishing or undoing an install a crash cut short.

**Errors.** `ErrorCode::Refused` if it is not a store or its journal cannot be read.

**Blocks.** While a job of this store runs, and on the disk: call it off a UI thread, or use the language's asynchronous form.

### `catalog` [#catalog]

### `remove` [#remove]

Removes the packs and the dependencies nothing else needs; returns what was removed.

**Errors.** `ErrorCode::Refused` if one is not installed or another pack needs it.

**Blocks.** While a job of this store runs, and on the disk: call it off a UI thread, or use the language's asynchronous form.

### `find` [#find]

The places named `query` in `engine` (one over a world pack the app ships, the installed packs, or both), best first, each with the catalog's packs that cover it: what to install for "Dubai". Runs offline on the stored catalog.

**Errors.** `ErrorCode::InvalidArgument` for a limit above `LIMIT_MAX`; `ErrorCode::Refused` if the stored catalog no longer verifies.

**Blocks.** While a job of this store runs, and on the disk: call it off a UI thread, or use the language's asynchronous form.

### `install` [#install]

Installs the packs with `options`, dependencies first, refreshing the catalog for their countries. Cancelled, it leaves the store as it was; the packs installed before the one cut stay installed.

**Errors.** `ErrorCode::InvalidArgument` for an unknown component or language tag, more than 8 languages, or an outline level above 255; the job's own errors are the job's.

### `install_pass` [#install_pass]

One pass of an install whose bytes a platform's own download service fetches, for downloads that must go on while the app is suspended. The pass reads each asset's ranges from files under `dir`, checks every byte as from any host, and its result lists what is still missing, one row per range: `pack`, `urls` (the asset on each mirror, one per line), `length` (the asset's), `start` and `end` (the range, end exclusive) and `file`, where to save those bytes. Fetch every listed range (an HTTP `Range` request for `bytes=start-(end-1)`), then run the pass again; a result with no rows means the packs are installed and their files under `dir` removed. A first install takes three passes.

**Errors.** `ErrorCode::InvalidArgument` as for `Store::install`, or for an empty `dir`; the job's own errors are the job's.

<Tabs groupId="lang" persist items={["Rust","Python","JavaScript","Swift","Java and Kotlin","Dart","Go","C","C++",".NET"]}>
<Tab value="Rust">
```rust
pub fn install_pass(&self, packs: &str, dir: &str, options: &InstallOptions) -> Result<Job>
```
</Tab>

<Tab value="Python">
```python

```
</Tab>

<Tab value="JavaScript">
```ts

```
</Tab>

<Tab value="Swift">
```swift

```
</Tab>

<Tab value="Java and Kotlin">
```java

```
</Tab>

<Tab value="Dart">
```dart

```

</Tab>

<Tab value="C">

</Tab>

<Tab value="C++">
```cpp

```
</Tab>

## Job [#job]

A store's long work on a thread of its own: its progress in bytes, a wait for the next change, a cancel, and its result.

**Job.** Each language builds its own idioms on these methods: a stream of progress, and the awaited result cancelling the job when the caller's task is cancelled.

### `wait_progress` [#wait_progress]

Waits until the progress moves past `seq` (from `seq`), the job ends, or `timeout_ms` passes; returns the sequence then. Polling with the last one returned sees every change.

**Blocks.** Until the job moves or ends: call it off a UI thread, or use the language's asynchronous form.

<Tabs groupId="lang" persist items={["Rust","Python","JavaScript","Swift","Java and Kotlin","Dart","Go","C","C++",".NET"]}>
<Tab value="Rust">
```rust
pub fn wait_progress(&self, seq: u64, timeout_ms: u32) -> u64
```
</Tab>

<Tab value="Python">
```python
def wait_progress(self, seq: int, timeout_ms: int) -> int: ...
```
</Tab>

<Tab value="JavaScript">
```ts
waitProgress(seq: number, timeoutMs: number): number;
```
</Tab>

<Tab value="Swift">
```swift
public func waitProgress(_ seq: UInt64, timeoutMs: UInt32) -> UInt64
```
</Tab>

<Tab value="Java and Kotlin">
```java
public long waitProgress(long seq, long timeoutMs);
```
</Tab>

<Tab value="Dart">
```dart
int waitProgress(int seq, int timeoutMs);
```
</Tab>

<Tab value="Go">
```go
func (h *Job) WaitProgress(seq uint64, timeoutMs uint32) uint64
```
</Tab>

<Tab value="C">
```c

```
</Tab>

<Tab value="C++">
```cpp

```
</Tab>

<Tab value=".NET">
```csharp

```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

### `result` [#result]

The job's result, waiting for it to end.

**Errors.** The job's: `ErrorCode::Network`, `ErrorCode::Refused`, `ErrorCode::Cancelled`, or `ErrorCode::Io` and `ErrorCode::Corrupt` for an engine's packs.

**Blocks.** Until the job moves or ends: call it off a UI thread, or use the language's asynchronous form.

# Types, constants and errors (/docs/reference/types)

## Options records [#options-records]

Every field's zero value is its default, so a record made with no fields set asks for the
defaults (in C, a null pointer does too). Each language spells a field
its own way: `focus_lat` is `focusLat` in JavaScript, Swift, Java, Kotlin and Dart, and
`FocusLat` in Go and C#.

### `SearchOptions` [#searchoptions]

How `Engine::search_with` ranks. Every field's zero value is its default.

| Field | Type | Default | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| `focus_lat` | `Option<f64>` | none | Prefer places near this latitude (with `focus_lon`): the user's location, or a point in their home country with a wide scale. |
| `focus_lon` | `Option<f64>` | none | The focus longitude; set with `focus_lat` or not at all. |
| `focus_scale_m` | `Option<f64>` | none | The distance in metres at which the focus gain halves (a place at the focus gains 30, one scale away 15); `None` is 50 km. |
| `strict` | `bool` | `false` | Rank by match tier first (exact, loose, prefix, one edit, substring, two edits, phonetic), then importance and focus, instead of one additive score. |

### `OpenOptions` [#openoptions]

How `Engine::open_file_with` and `Engine::open_bytes_with` open a pack. Every field's zero value is its default.

| Field | Type | Default | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| `priority` | `i32` | `0` | Precedence over the other packs: a higher one wins where packs disagree (default 0). |
| `verify` | `Verify` | `Lazy` | When sections are verified. |
| `load` | `Load` | `Map` | How a file is loaded; ignored for bytes. |
| `outline_level` | `Option<u32>` | none | The deepest admin level whose outlines are read, in a pack that splits its outlines by level: admin units below it are not found at a point, and their outlines are not loaded. `None` reads every level. |
| `outline_tolerance_m` | `u32` | `0` | The largest simplification of the outlines read, in metres, when the pack has coarser outlines; 0 is full resolution. Admin units at a point may then differ within that distance of a border. |
| `components` | `String` | empty | The components the pack holds, by name and comma-separated (`point,names,search`), for a pack installed in part; what they need is added. Empty for a whole pack. A query that needs a component left out answers nothing, or `MissingComponent` where it cannot. |
| `languages` | `String` | empty | The languages whose names and search sections are read, as comma-separated BCP 47 tags (`en,ne`), at most 8; a language without a part of its own reads the pack's shared part. Empty reads every language. |

### `InstallOptions` [#installoptions]

What `Store::install` takes of each pack. Every field's zero value is its default: the whole pack.

| Field | Type | Default | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| `components` | `String` | empty | The components, by name and comma-separated (`point,names,search`); what they need is added. Empty for every component. |
| `languages` | `String` | empty | The languages besides the base names, as comma-separated BCP 47 tags (`en,ne`), at most 8. Empty for every language. |
| `outline_level` | `Option<u32>` | none | The deepest admin level of the one outline part installed; `None` for every outline. |
| `outline_tolerance_m` | `u32` | `0` | The tolerance in metres of that outline part; 0 is full resolution. |
| `pin` | `bool` | `false` | Keeps the packs when room is made. |

## Enums [#enums]

### `Verify` [#verify]

When a pack's sections are verified against their hashes.

| Variant | Value | What |
|---|--:|---|
| `Lazy` | 0 | On first use: each section, or each 16 KiB block of a large one, is checked the first time a query reads it. Opening costs only the head checks. |
| `Eager` | 1 | Every section when the pack opens. |
| `Trusted` | 2 | Never: only for bytes already verified, by the store's installer for instance. |

### `Load` [#load]

How a pack file is loaded.

| Variant | Value | What |
|---|--:|---|
| `Map` | 0 | Map the file into memory where the platform can, read it otherwise. The file must not be written over while it is open. |
| `Read` | 1 | Read the whole file into memory: for files the application does not own. |

## Constants [#constants]

| Constant | Value | What |
|---|--:|---|
| `SAMPLE_ROWS_MAX` | 1000000 | Most rows `sample_rows` builds in one call. |
| `LIMIT_MAX` | 10000 | Most places one query returns. |
| `COARSEST_LOD` | 6 | The coarsest level of detail `Engine::boundary` reads; 0 is full resolution. |

## Errors [#errors]

A call that fails gives one of these codes and a message, the same in every language. Each
language raises it in its own way:

| Language | A failure is |
|---|---|
| Rust | `teigeodata_api::Error`, with `code` (an `ErrorCode`) and `message` |
| Python | `TeiGeodataError`, or its subclass for the code: `InvalidArgumentError`, `CancelledError`, `InternalError`, `IoError`, `CorruptError`, `MissingComponentError`, `NetworkError`, `RefusedError` |
| JavaScript | an `Error` whose `code` is the code's name, such as `"InvalidArgument"` |
| Swift | a thrown `TeiGeodataError`, with `code` (`TeiGeodataError.Code`) |
| Java and Kotlin | `TeiGeodataException` (unchecked), or its subclass for the code, such as `TeiGeodataException.Cancelled`; `code()` gives the value |
| Dart | the sealed `TeiGeodataException`: `InvalidArgumentException`, `CancelledException`, `InternalException`, `IoException`, `CorruptException`, `MissingComponentException`, `NetworkException`, `RefusedException` |
| Go | an `error` holding a `*teigeodata.Error`; test it with `errors.Is(err, teigeodata.CodeInvalidArgument)` |
| C | the code as the return value (0 is success); `tg_last_error` gives the message on the same thread |
| C++ | `teigeodata::Error` (a `std::runtime_error`), with `code()` |
| .NET | `TeiGeodataException`, with `Code` (an `ErrorCode`) |

| Code | Value | Meaning |
|---|--:|---|
| `InvalidArgument` | 1 | An argument is outside its documented range. |
| `Cancelled` | 2 | A callback asked to stop. |
| `Internal` | 3 | A bug inside teigeodata (a panic caught at the boundary, or a broken invariant). |
| `Io` | 4 | A file could not be read. |
| `Corrupt` | 5 | The bytes are not a valid pack, or a section does not match its hash. |
| `MissingComponent` | 6 | The query needs a component of a pack that is not installed: install it, or ask a pack that has it. |
| `Network` | 7 | The network failed: no mirror answered, or the connection broke. Try again later. |
| `Refused` | 8 | The store refused: the catalog did not verify, a pack is not in it or not installed, a pack another needs, or the store's files cannot be written. |

# HTTP server (/docs/servers/http)

`tgd serve` puts the packs behind an HTTP API: every query as a `GET` route, native JSON or
GeoJSON, and Nominatim-compatible `/search`, `/reverse` and `/lookup` so existing clients work
unchanged. It is one process with no database: the packs are memory-mapped, and on Nepal it
answers about 9,000 requests per second for the heaviest route (a large boundary) and 40,000 to
90,000 for the others, at 16 connections on one machine ([measured](/docs/data/measured#server-load)
by `cargo xtask load`, with a budget the load test enforces).

<Callout title="Every example on this page ran">
The requests below are part of the [command-line tour](https://github.com/teispace/teigeodata/blob/main/site/examples/cli/tour.sh),
which starts the server on the released pack, sends them with curl, and checks the answers.
</Callout>

## Start it [#start-it]

```sh
tgd serve --pack world-np-lite.tgd
# serving on http://127.0.0.1:8080
```

| Option | Default | What |
|---|---|---|
| `--listen <addr:port>` | `127.0.0.1:8080` | Where to listen; port 0 picks a free one. Loopback only unless you name another address. |
| `--pack <file>` | the store's packs | A pack to serve; repeat for several. Given, it replaces the store: only these packs are served, and nothing is followed. |
| `--store <dir>` | the platform's data directory | Serve the store's installed packs, and follow it as packs are installed or updated. |
| `--follow <seconds>` | 5 | How often to read the store's journal; 0 never. |
| `--timeout <seconds>` | 10 | A request taking longer is answered `unavailable`. |
| `--max-connections <n>` | 1024 | The most connections kept open; more wait until one closes. |
| `--max-in-flight <n>` | 256 | The most requests answered at once; one more is answered `unavailable` at once, with `Retry-After: 1`. |
| `--cors-origin <origin>` | none | An origin browsers may call from; repeat for several. CORS is off by default. |
| `--allow-install` | off | Let MCP clients install catalog packs into the store. |

```sh title="tour.sh"
curl -s "$URL/health"
```

```json title="Response"
{"status":"ok","layers":1}
```

## Native routes [#native-routes]

Every route is `GET /v1/<query>` with query parameters, and answers
`{"results": [...], "attribution": "..."}` (or `"result"` for one value). `limit` defaults to 10.

| Route | Answers |
|---|---|
| `/v1/search` | Places matching a name, best first, with `score`. |
| `/v1/get` | One place; `names=1` adds every name with its language. |
| `/v1/lookup` | Places by ID, in the order asked. |
| `/v1/reverse` | The nearest places with `meters`, `bearing` and `inside`. |
| `/v1/near` | The places nearest a place. |
| `/v1/admin` | The admin units holding the point, country first. |
| `/v1/hierarchy` | A place's ancestors, parent first. |
| `/v1/children` | A place's children. |
| `/v1/tz` | The timezone with its offset, abbreviation and DST flag at `t`. |
| `/v1/elevation` | The terrain height, its datum, source and grid spacing. |
| `/v1/distance` | The great-circle distance and initial bearing. |
| `/v1/postal` | Postal codes and their places. |
| `/v1/boundary` | A unit's outline as GeoJSON. |
| `/v1/coverage` | The catalog's packs that cover a point (a server over a store). |
| `/packs` | The packs served, with their components, places and attribution. |
| `/health` | `{"status": "ok", "layers": n}`. |

Every parameter of every route, with its bounds and default, is in the [HTTP API reference](/docs/reference/http).

Search:

```sh title="tour.sh"
curl -s "$URL/v1/search?q=Pokhara&limit=2"
```

```json title="Response"
{"results":[
{"id":"tgd:np/1xhb","name":"Pokhara","kind":"settlement","admin_level":0,"lat":28.26689,"lon":83.968,"elevation":1006,"elevation_source":"model","parent":"tgd:np/1xnr","timezone":"Asia/Kathmandu","score":132},
{"id":"tgd:np/1xnr","name":"Pokhara","kind":"admin","admin_level":3,"lat":28.209407,"lon":83.981817,"elevation":842,"elevation_source":"model","parent":"tgd:np/295c","timezone":"Asia/Kathmandu","score":105}
],"attribution":"Made with Natural Earth (https://www.naturalearthdata.com), public domain\nGeoNames (https://www.geonames.org), CC BY 4.0\nTime zones: IANA Time Zone Database 2026f (public domain)\nWikidata (https://www.wikidata.org), CC0 1.0\nUnicode CLDR (https://cldr.unicode.org), Copyright © 1991-2026 Unicode, Inc., under the Unicode License v3\nLocal Government Directory, Ministry of Panchayati Raj, Government of India (https://lgdirectory.gov.in)\nAdministrative boundaries: Survey Department of Nepal and UN Resident Coordinator's Office in Nepal, via OCHA HDX (cod-ab-npl), CC BY-IGO 3.0\nElevation: NASADEM, NASA JPL and LP DAAC\nBuildings: Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints, CDLA-Permissive-2.0 (https://cdla.dev/permissive-2-0/)\nBuildings: Google Open Buildings v3 (Sirko et al. 2021, arXiv:2107.12283), CC BY 4.0\nCentral Bureau of Statistics (now National Statistics Office), Nepal, via Open Data Nepal (https://opendatanepal.com), Creative Commons Attribution"}
```

## GeoJSON [#geojson]

Add `format=geojson` to any route that answers places, and the answer is a FeatureCollection
(RFC 7946) that MapLibre, Leaflet, OpenLayers and QGIS read directly:

```sh title="tour.sh"
curl -s "$URL/v1/admin?lat=28.2096&lon=83.9856&format=geojson"
```

```json title="Response"
{"type":"FeatureCollection","attribution":"Made with Natural Earth (https://www.naturalearthdata.com), public domain\nGeoNames (https://www.geonames.org), CC BY 4.0\nTime zones: IANA Time Zone Database 2026f (public domain)\nWikidata (https://www.wikidata.org), CC0 1.0\nUnicode CLDR (https://cldr.unicode.org), Copyright © 1991-2026 Unicode, Inc., under the Unicode License v3\nLocal Government Directory, Ministry of Panchayati Raj, Government of India (https://lgdirectory.gov.in)\nAdministrative boundaries: Survey Department of Nepal and UN Resident Coordinator's Office in Nepal, via OCHA HDX (cod-ab-npl), CC BY-IGO 3.0\nElevation: NASADEM, NASA JPL and LP DAAC\nBuildings: Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints, CDLA-Permissive-2.0 (https://cdla.dev/permissive-2-0/)\nBuildings: Google Open Buildings v3 (Sirko et al. 2021, arXiv:2107.12283), CC BY 4.0\nCentral Bureau of Statistics (now National Statistics Office), Nepal, via Open Data Nepal (https://opendatanepal.com), Creative Commons Attribution","features":[
{"type":"Feature","id":"tgd:np/1wmc","geometry":{"type":"Point","coordinates":[84.0,28.0]},"properties":{"id":"tgd:np/1wmc","name":"Nepal","kind":"country","admin_level":0,"elevation":1046,"elevation_source":"model","parent":null,"timezone":"Asia/Kathmandu","iso_code":"NP"}},

{"type":"Feature","id":"tgd:np/295c","geometry":{"type":"Point","coordinates":[83.970886,28.345513]},"properties":{"id":"tgd:np/295c","name":"Kaski","kind":"admin","admin_level":2,"elevation":1231,"elevation_source":"model","parent":"tgd:np/2922","timezone":"Asia/Kathmandu"}},
{"type":"Feature","id":"tgd:np/1xnr","geometry":{"type":"Point","coordinates":[83.981817,28.209407]},"properties":{"id":"tgd:np/1xnr","name":"Pokhara","kind":"admin","admin_level":3,"elevation":842,"elevation_source":"model","parent":"tgd:np/295c","timezone":"Asia/Kathmandu"}}
```
